learning: Iteration 5 (y = 0.05 m) was the first geometry to lift s-bend progress above 0.04 (to 0.1475) with oscillation below 0.16. Iterations 2 to 4 at y = 0.03 m, under kp, drivetrain and pitch changes, stayed at 0.04. Line loss on the s-bend and slalom returned to 1.0 at y = 0.05 m, and this is the main open question.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's y = 0.07 m forward-lead test on the iteration 5 platform. The controller is unchanged from iteration 5 so the race isolates the sensor offset.
rationale: Iteration 5 moved all seven 16 mm contiguous sensors from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.05 m, with the iteration 2 drivetrain (wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg) and controller (kp 5.0). S-bend progress rose from 0.04 to 0.1475, and steering_oscillation stayed at 0.1366, below the 0.16 trigger. Forward lead is therefore the first lever to move the s-bend, which kp (iteration 3), pitch and drivetrain (iteration 4) did not. Iteration 5 still shows one line-loss event on the s-bend and slalom, and slalom max_error of 0.0661 m. The oval is clean at 0 line loss and 0.115 progress. The Builder's intent is to test a further lead of y = 0.07 m. The Integrator's rule says that when s-bend progress rises with oscillation below 0.16, keep the forward offset and test more lead, so I adopt it. I keep the controller identical to iteration 5 (kp 5.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights proportional to x with a positive signal steering left) so that this race isolates the forward offset. I keep the 16 mm contiguous layout at x = ±0.048 m, because iteration 4 showed that a 20 mm pitch cut slalom progress. I expect s-bend progress above 0.1475 and steering_oscillation below 0.16. Line loss on the s-bend and slalom may persist or worsen, since the sensors see the bend earlier. These are predictions, not measurements.
